To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the conjugate 2 (para-substituted) shows higher duplex-DNA-binding affinity and a higher change in the DNA-DNA-binding efficiency upon photoillumination compared with its 3 (ortho-substituted) counterpart.

the conjugate with 4,4-dialkoxyazophenyl moiety as the core exhibited a higher affinity for duplex DNA than the 2, 2'-dialkylated counterpart, and the former conjugate also showed a higher photoisomerization rate than the latter.
we have developed new azobenzene-containing distamycin dimmers that show photoisomerization in solution and that their DNA-binding efficiency can be altered by the photoisomerization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, synthesis, and photophysical and DNA-binding studies of two isomeric azobenzene-based conjugates, which were tethered to both termini of distamycin.
the synthesis and characterization of two new photoisomerizable, distamycin-based conjugates, 2 and 3, and with their duplex-DNA-binding and photoisomerization properties.
the design of new azobenzene-based DNA-binding agents that can be photocontrolled and can be used in the design of molecular devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the location of the distamycin moieties around the azobenzene moiets plays a crucial role in the photophysical properties of these conjugates and in their DNA-binding efficiency.
the photoisomerization of the azobenzene core of distamycin-2,2'-azobenzene-2,2' distamycin conjugate 3 was not accompanied by any change in its binding efficiency to duplex DNA.

the location of the distamycin moiety around the central azobenzene moi-ety is crucial for the DNA-binding affinity of the conjugates, and that the conjugate with the distamycin units attached to the para-positions of the central azobenzenes showed the highest DNA-binding affinity and the largest changes in DNA binding upon photoisomerizations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the photoisomerization of these azobenzene-containing distamycin conjugates in solution can be controlled by their molecular architecture and the position of the substituent on the azobenzene core.

a change of the molecular architecture of the conjugate around the azobenzene core can influence the rate and activation energy barrier for the cis to trans back isomerization of the conjugates in solution and the change in the DNA binding efficiency upon photo isomerization.

the photoisomerizable azobenzene moieties in these distamycin-based conjugates could be utilized as a light-switching element for the control of DNA binding and DNA-binding efficiency of these conjugates.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the photochemical properties and DNA-binding affinity of these azobenzene-containing distamycin dimmers are strongly dependent on the molecular architecture of the azobenzene unit and the location of substituents around the azobenzylene core.
the location of the distamycin moieties around the core azo group is a key factor that influences both the photophysical and the duplex-DNA-binding characteristics of these systems.
the conjugates based on 4'-dialkozyazobenzene as the central core are more suitable candidates for the development of photoisomerizable DNA intercalating agents.
